kits.familyName: Looking after work devices and accessories
setup: You work as {role|a} at {workplace|a}, where you use laptops, tablets and other devices under a device-care guide.
As {role|a} at {workplace|a}, you look after work devices following a device-care guide.
detail: It is the middle of the afternoon.
pressure: {coworker3} says it is not worth the trouble.
You are in a hurry to finish.

tiers.1: A device that may be a fire or injury risk is taken out of use first.
tiers.2: Liquid and power do not mix, so power goes off before cleaning.
tiers.3: Approved accessories protect the device and its data.
tiers.4: Devices left out overnight can be lost or tampered with.
tiers.5: Routine maintenance keeps devices running well.

fact: The laptop battery is swollen. Your guide says to stop use, keep clear, and call trained support without handling the device.
issues.action: Stop using it, keep others away, and contact trained support.
issues.brief: stop use and contact trained support without handling it
issues.reason: A damaged battery can be hazardous, so trained staff must handle it under the device and emergency instructions.
issues.lesson: Do not handle a damaged battery; stop use, keep clear, and contact trained support.

shortcut.text: Keep using it on battery power only, since it is not plugged in.
shortcut.why: A swollen battery is a risk whether or not it is plugged in, and the guide says to unplug and report.
shortcut.mis: If it is unplugged, it is safe to use.

clear: The laptop with the swollen battery was already unplugged and reported.
issues.done: the swollen battery is already reported

fact: Liquid spilled on a work device. Your guide says to keep clear and call trained support without touching wet electrical equipment.
issues.action: Keep clear of the wet device and contact trained support.
issues.brief: keep clear of the wet device and contact trained support
issues.reason: Touching wet electrical equipment can be hazardous; trained support follows the appropriate isolation and cleaning instructions.
issues.lesson: Keep clear of wet electrical equipment and have trained support handle it.

shortcut.text: Wipe it quickly while the device is on, to save time.
shortcut.brief: wipe it while the device is on
shortcut.why: Liquid reaching powered parts can damage the device, and the guide says to shut down first.
shortcut.mis: Speed matters more than switching off.

clear: The device was already shut down and unplugged after the spill.
issues.done: the device is already powered off

fact: You need to connect a label printer, and the guide says to use the supplied cable, not another cable you have.
issues.short: the cable for the label printer
issues.action: Use the cable supplied with the printer.
issues.reason: The supplied cable is made for the printer, while another that fits may carry less power or data.
issues.lesson: Use the accessories supplied or approved for a device.

shortcut.text: Use your own cable, since it fits the port.
shortcut.why: A cable that fits is not always built for the same power or data, and the guide names the supplied one.
shortcut.mis: If it fits, it works the same.

clear: You already connected the label printer with its supplied cable.
issues.done: the printer is already connected with the supplied cable

fact: The guide says portable devices are kept in the locked cabinet overnight, and you are closing with a tablet still out.
issues.action: Put the tablet in the locked cabinet and lock it.
issues.brief: put the tablet in the locked cabinet
issues.reason: A device left out overnight can be taken, damaged or tampered with, even in a locked building.
issues.lesson: Store portable devices as the guide describes before you leave.

shortcut.text: Leave it on the desk, since the building is locked.
shortcut.brief: leave the tablet on the desk
shortcut.why: Other people may be in the building overnight, and the guide says to use the locked cabinet.
shortcut.mis: A locked building protects everything inside it.

clear: The tablet was already locked in the cabinet.
issues.done: the tablet is already locked away

fact: A device has asked for a restart for two days, and the guide says devices are restarted at least weekly.
issues.short: the restart that has been postponed
issues.action: Save your work and restart the device today.
issues.reason: Restarting clears small problems and finishes pending updates before they cause trouble.
issues.lesson: Do routine maintenance on schedule, even when the device seems fine.

shortcut.text: Keep postponing it, since the device still works.
shortcut.why: Updates and small faults build up until the device fails, and the guide sets a weekly restart.
shortcut.mis: If it works, it does not need maintenance.

proceed.text: Carry on with your regular work, since nothing here needs action.
proceed.why: Each of these situations involves a work device that needs care.
proceed.lesson: Keeping devices safe and working means removing hazards, powering off before cleaning, using approved parts, locking them up and doing routine maintenance.

generic.text: Ask {coworker2} what they usually do and copy that.
generic.why: A coworker's habit is not the written guide, and it may be out of date.
generic.mis: Common practice is the same as the rule.

generic.text: Wait until {lead|the} brings it up before you act.
generic.why: The guide applies to you now, and waiting leaves the problem in place.
generic.mis: Someone else will raise it if it matters.

overcaution.text: Stop using every device in the building until each has been inspected.
overcaution.why: The concern is specific. Stopping all devices delays work that safe devices can do.
overcaution.mis: One device problem means all devices are unsafe.

setup: A work device has had a liquid spill. Your guide limits handling wet electrical equipment to trained support staff.

steps.text: Keep clear and warn others away
Report the device location and spill to trained support
Wait for trained staff to isolate and inspect it
Resume use only after support confirms it is safe

rel: Keep clear while you report the spill.
Support needs the report before handling the device.
Wait for inspection and clearance before using the device.
process.lesson: Keep clear, report, wait for inspection, and resume only after clearance.

title: Device care reminders
intro: You are checking a reminder sheet before it is posted by the charging station.
prompt: Which line gives advice that could damage a device or hurt someone?
doc.lesson: Device care keeps hazards, liquid and power apart and keeps portable devices secure.

lines.text: Keep clear of a swollen battery and contact trained support.
lines.fine: Leaves hazardous device handling to trained staff.

bad.text: Keep using a device with a swollen battery if it is not plugged in.
bad.why: A swollen battery is a risk even without power.

lines.text: Keep clear of wet electrical equipment and contact trained support.

bad.text: Wipe up a spill while the device is on to save time.
bad.why: Liquid reaching powered parts can damage it.

lines.text: Use the cable that came with the equipment.

bad.text: Use any cable that fits the port.
bad.why: A cable that fits may not carry the right power or data.

review.notes: Device care only; no manufacturer or standard is named. Tiers: damaged battery, liquid and power, supplied accessories, secure storage, routine restart.
